title: 第103章 正气不灭赓续传承第102章 藏在风骨藏在正心
slug: 我被系统坑成了造物主
content_zh:
姬云天听着众人的唏嘘，将轩辕学院办赛传道的经历说与众人听，又提出要联合联盟，在苍天大世界各州分建文道分院，给各地散修文者提供落脚修学的地方，再刊印文道先贤典籍，免费发放给各地好文道之人，听得一众耆老频频点头，原本愁云惨淡的议事堂，渐渐又生了明亮的气色。
姬云天与众老商议妥了各项章程，临走前，联盟的盟主拉着姬云天的手，将一枚传承千年的文道印鉴交到他手里，叹道：“这印鉴，我们守了一辈子，现在终于交到能让它重新发光的人手里了，我死也能闭眼去见先贤了。”
姬云天接过印鉴，只觉入手温热，印鉴里流转着千年不散的浩然气，他对着一众耆老深深一揖，朗声道：“诸位放心，姬云天这一生，必守文道风骨，传薪火不息，定不辱使命。”
联盟的盟主道：“我会把这里的一百余个先贤碑派人送到轩辕学院，只留几个作为纪念。”
姬云天点了点头，对着盟主深深一躬。
离开落星原时，姬云天回头望去，只见漫山古柏在风中沙沙作响，像是无数先贤在低声附和，远处的天际，正有一片温润的文气青云缓缓升起，和当初轩辕学院上空的那片，遥遥连成了一片。
走了半月路程，姬云天并未直接回转轩辕学院，反倒顺着各州地界一路慢行，沿路寻访那些隐于山野的文道修士。这些修士多是独来独往，守着几卷古籍在陋巷山中苦熬，不少人连糊口都难，却始终不肯放下手中的笔。
姬云天每到一处，便留下一些修行资源，又将分院建立的消息说与他们，邀他们前去修学论道，不少人听了之后，当场便哭出声，说这辈子从没想过还能有同好一起论道的一天。
一路行来，姬云天也收拢了许多流落民间的孤本古籍，有些还是早已失传的先贤文集，他小心收在储物戒里，想着回去之后便一同刊印出去，不让这些学问就此埋没。这日走到苍澜域青梧城地界，便寻了一间山中小庙歇脚，刚生了火，就见庙门被推开，一个背着书筐的年轻秀才走了进来，身上的衣服打了好几个补丁，却把怀里的几卷书护得干干净净。
那秀才见了姬云天，先是规规矩矩行了礼，才敢在火堆边坐下烤火，姬云天见他书筐上挂着一块刻着文道联盟标记的木牌，便笑着问他可知道此次文道复兴的事，那秀才眼睛一下子亮了，说他早就听说了，正赶着去落星原，想要投奔联盟，只是盘缠不够，只能一路步行过去。
姬云天又问他，修文道这么苦，怎么还愿意坚持，秀才摸了摸怀里的书，认真道：“我祖父是修文道的，父亲也是，他们说，哪怕只有一个人读，这些书也不能断，我总得接着走下去。”
姬云天看着少年眼里的光，想起了当初姬云天对文强说的那句话，心里又是温热又是感慨，文道的传承，本来就是这样一代一代，靠着这些普通人咬着牙撑下来的，也是靠着他们一步一个脚印走到当下，虽未鼎盛，却依旧坚韧。
第二日起身，姬云天给秀才留下了足够的盘缠，让秀才不必去落星原，可以去轩辕学院直接去文道院报道，又将将他推荐给文强，留言了一个玉简让他带上，安排他参与典籍校勘的活儿，少年千恩万谢地走了，姬云天站在山门口望着他的背影，只觉那一步步走的，就是文道的前路。
等姬云天回到轩辕学院，已经是三个月以后的了，各州的文道分部都已经按照商议好的章程建了起来，无数散居各地的文道修士纷纷前去投奔，姬云天常可以看到那些文道修士激动的样子，也看到那些行进在山河之中奔赴向往的文道修士们，原本冷清的文道，渐渐又热闹了起来。
文强拿着登记的名册来见姬云天，笑着说，光是第一个月，前来登记的文道修士就比过去百年联盟收录的还要多，不少年轻子弟，都愿意放下快进的武道，沉下心来修文道养正气了。姬云天翻着厚厚的名册，看着上面一个个或熟悉或陌生的名字，只觉胸中那股浩然气久久不散。
又过了三个月，第一届文道盛会如期在轩辕学院开幕，这一次来的修士，比半年前多了足足十倍，从满头白发的耆老到总角少年，挤满了整个轩辕广场，人人脸上都带着光，开口谈的是文道，闭口说的是传承。姬云天站在高台上，看着台下攒动的人头，想起三年前第一次大赛时，文道修士寥寥无几的样子，不由笑了，身旁的姬飞雪轻声道：“你看，当初你说要文道兴，现在真的兴了。”
姬云天望着天际那片越来越辽阔的文气青云，高声对着台下道：“诸位，文道兴衰，不在天道，不在先贤，在于你我，在于每一个愿意提笔的后来人！只要我们手里的笔不丢，心中的正气不灭，这文道风骨，就永远赓续传承！”话音落下，全场齐声呼应，声浪直冲云霄，把那片温润的青云，染得越发金黄明亮，千百年后，这声呼应，依然在苍天大世界的天地间，久久回荡。
文道盛会落幕后，轩辕学院留了半月时间供各地来的修士交流论道。每日清晨，轩辕广场的石台上都有修士开讲，从最基础的养气炼文，到高深的以文化道，讲者倾囊相授，听者凝神静记，连学院外的林间石径上，都随处可见凑在一起交换心得的身影，他们带着对文道的崇敬与向往，口中尽显对文道的热忱。
姬云天这几日没登台讲道，只穿着普通的青衫混在人群里，听着这些来自五湖四海的修士说自己对文道的感悟，积极地倾听着各界文道修士的见解，偶尔遇上迷茫的年轻人问起问题，也悄悄提点两句，没露自己的身份。
这日傍晚，他顺着山径走到学院后山的先贤碑林，却见一个十六七岁的少年正蹲在一块残破的石碑前，皱着眉临摹碑上的字迹，面前的石桌上铺着一张粗糙的麻纸，笔也是磨得快没了毛的旧笔，可少年一笔一划，写得格外认真。

content_en:
Ji Yuntian listened to everyone's sighs and told everyone about Xuanyuan College's experience in organizing competitions and evangelism. He also proposed to unite an alliance to build literary branches in various states of Cangtian World to provide a place for casual practitioners from all over the world to study. He would then publish the classics of literary sages and distribute them for free to people who are good at literature everywhere. Hearing the elders nodding frequently, the originally gloomy meeting hall gradually became brighter again.
Ji Yuntian discussed various articles of association with the elders. Before leaving, the leader of the alliance took Ji Yuntian's hand and handed him a cultural seal that had been passed down for thousands of years. He sighed: "We have guarded this seal for a lifetime, and now it is finally in the hands of someone who can make it shine again. I will be able to close my eyes and go see the sages even after I die."
Ji Yuntian took the seal and felt it was warm. The aura of grandeur that had lasted for thousands of years was flowing in the seal. He bowed deeply to the elders and said loudly: "Don't worry, everyone, Ji Yuntian will abide by the integrity of the literary tradition in his life, continue to pass on the legacy, and will definitely fulfill his mission."
The leader of the alliance said: "I will send more than a hundred sage monuments here to Xuanyuan College, leaving only a few as souvenirs."
Ji Yuntian nodded and bowed deeply to the alliance leader.
When leaving Luoxingyuan, Ji Yuntian looked back and saw ancient cypresses rustling in the wind, as if countless sages were whispering in agreement. In the distant sky, a warm and elegant blue cloud was slowly rising, and it was connected to the one above Xuanyuan College.
After walking for half a month, Ji Yuntian did not return directly to Xuanyuan College. Instead, he walked slowly along the boundaries of the states, looking for the literary monks hiding in the mountains along the way. Most of these monks lived alone, languishing in the back alleys and mountains guarding a few volumes of ancient books. Many of them had difficulty making ends meet, but they still refused to put down their pens.
Everywhere Ji Yuntian went, he left some spiritual resources, told them about the establishment of the branch, and invited them to study and discuss Taoism. After hearing this, many people cried on the spot, saying that they had never thought that one day they would be able to discuss Taoism with fellow practitioners.
Along the way, Ji Yuntian also collected many ancient ancient books that were lost among the people, some of which were long-lost collections of sages. He carefully kept them in his storage ring, thinking that he would publish them together when he returned to prevent these knowledge from being buried. This day, when I walked to the boundary of Qingwu City in Canglan Region, I found a small temple in the mountain to rest. As soon as I lit a fire, I saw the temple door was pushed open, and a young scholar carrying a book basket walked in. His clothes were patched several times, but he kept the books in his arms clean.
When the scholar met Ji Yuntian, he bowed politely before he dared to sit down by the fire to warm himself. When Ji Yuntian saw a wooden sign with the logo of the Literary and Taoist Alliance hanging on his book basket, he smiled and asked him if he knew about the revival of the Literary and Taoist Alliance. The scholar's eyes suddenly lit up and he said that he had heard about it a long time ago and was on his way to Luoxingyuan. He wanted to defect to the alliance, but he didn't have enough money, so he had to walk all the way.
Ji Yuntian asked him again why he was still willing to persist in cultivating the Tao of Literature when it was so hard. The scholar touched the book in his arms and said seriously: "My grandfather is a practitioner of the Tao of Literature, and so is my father. They said that even if only one person reads these books, these books cannot be cut off. I have to continue on."
Ji Yuntian looked at the light in the young man's eyes and remembered what Ji Yuntian said to Wen Qiang. His heart felt warm and emotional at the same time. The inheritance of literature was originally like this from generation to generation. It was sustained by these ordinary people gritting their teeth. It was also relying on them to reach the present step by step. Although it was not at its peak, it was still tenacious.
When he got up on the second day, Ji Yuntian left enough money for the scholar so that he didn't have to go to Luoxingyuan. He could go to Xuanyuan College and report directly to the Literary Academy. He recommended him to Wen Qiang and left a jade slip for him to take with him, arranging for him to participate in the collation of classics. The young man left with great gratitude. Ji Yuntian stood at the gate of the mountain and looked at his back. He felt that stepWalking step by step is the path forward for literature.
By the time Ji Yuntian returned to Xuanyuan College, it was already three months later. The literary branches in each state had been established in accordance with the agreed charter. Countless liberal arts monks scattered around the country had gone to seek refuge. Ji Yuntian could often see the excitement of those liberal arts monks, and he could also see those liberal arts monks marching through the mountains and rivers to pursue their dreams. The originally deserted liberal arts gradually became lively again.
Wen Qiang came to Ji Yuntian with the registration list and said with a smile that in the first month alone, more literary cultivators came to register than those registered by the alliance in the past hundred years. Many young disciples are willing to put aside their fast-paced martial arts and settle down to cultivate their moral character. Ji Yuntian flipped through the thick roster, looking at the familiar and unfamiliar names on it, and felt the awe-inspiring aura in his chest lingering for a long time.
Three months later, the first Literary and Dao Festival opened as scheduled at Xuanyuan College. This time, there were ten times more monks than half a year ago. From the white-haired elders to the young men in charge, the whole Xuanyuan Square was packed. Everyone's face was shining. They talked about Literary Dao when they opened their mouths, and inheritance when they kept silent. Ji Yuntian stood on the high platform, looking at the crowds of people in the audience. He recalled how there were only a few literary monks during the first competition three years ago, and couldn't help but smile. Ji Feixue beside him said softly: "Look, you said you wanted to be civilized, but now it is really popular."
Ji Yuntian looked at the ever-expanding clouds of literary talent in the sky, and said loudly to the audience: "Everyone, the rise and fall of literary education does not depend on the way of heaven, nor on the sages, but on you and me, and on everyone who is willing to pick up the pen! As long as we don't lose the pen in our hands, the righteousness in our hearts will be As long as this literary spirit is immortal, it will continue to be passed on forever!" After the words fell, the whole audience echoed in unison, and the sound surged into the sky, dyeing the warm blue clouds more and more golden and bright. Thousands of years later, this echo is still echoing in the heaven and earth of the world.
After the literary and Taoist event ended, Xuanyuan College set aside half a month for monks from all over the country to exchange ideas and discuss Taoism. Every morning, there are monks giving lectures on the stone platform in Xuanyuan Square, from the most basic Qi nourishing and literary refinement to the advanced cultural Tao. The lecturers teach each other with all their knowledge, and the listeners memorize silently. Even on the stone paths in the forest outside the academy, you can see people gathering together to exchange experiences. They bring their reverence and yearning for the Tao of literature, and their enthusiasm for the Tao of literature is evident in their mouths.
Ji Yuntian did not preach on the stage in the past few days. He only wore an ordinary green shirt and mingled with the crowd. He listened to these monks from all over the world talk about their insights on the literary world. He actively listened to the opinions of the literary monks from all walks of life. Occasionally, when he met a confused young man who asked questions, he quietly raised a few words without revealing his identity.
That evening, he walked along the mountain path to the forest of sage monuments at the back of the college. He saw a sixteen or seventeen-year-old boy squatting in front of a broken stone tablet, frowning and copying the handwriting on the tablet. The stone table in front of him was covered with a piece of rough hemp paper. The pen was also an old pen that had almost lost its hair, but the young man wrote every stroke with great care.
